thread:
Maya: Hey — noticed in the compact table variant the action buttons get partially covered by toasts when a row error appears. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.dev/ux/compact-toast-overlap.png

Jon: ah yeah I can repro. Happens when spacing token is set to --spacing-compact and toast uses the default bottom margin. :thinking_face:

Sam: is this the same issue as earlier where toasts float at z-index 800 and table row controls are 900?

Maya: I checked — the table's action popovers are 900 but the inline buttons are in the flow and their container has no stacking context, so the toast visually sits on top.

Alessandra: quick idea: either raise the toast z-index or give the table a local stacking context (e.g., transform: translateZ(0) or position: relative + z-index). Prefer not to raise toast globally since toasts should float above everything else.

Jon: agree, raising toasts globally is risky. Could we instead add a token for component stacking, like --z-surface-controls that defaults above toast for interactive surfaces? then components that need to sit above toasts opt-in.

Oliver: That sounds fine, but it makes the opt-in burden on components. Another approach: change toast placement for compact lists to be anchored to the console root with margin-bottom: calc(var(--spacing-compact) * 2) so it doesn't overlap controls.

Sam: Both are viable. From an accessibility POV we should also ensure the toast doesn't trap focus or hide the control that just received focus. If a user triggers an inline action, the resulting toast must not obscure the control or cover its label.

Maya: Good call. For now I can patch the compact table to add a small bottom padding token when inline actions present: --table-inline-action-offset: var(--spacing-compact);

Jon: If we do that, add a short comment in the CSS module and a test case in the visual regression suite: compact table + toast = no overlap. I'll file the ticket.

DesignBot: New design task created: D-1129 — Compact table toast overlap. Assignees: @Maya, @Jon. Due: 2026-04-02.

Alessandra: Also a copy nit — the toast copy for save success currently says "Saved". Can we update to "Changes saved" to be clearer in dense contexts? Tiny UX improvement for screen reader announcements too.

Maya: yes will change copy in next PR. Also adding aria-live="polite" on the toast region so SR will announce the more descriptive text.

Oliver: One more: please ensure the token naming avoids "compact" in global API. Use density tokens (e.g., --spacing-density-tight) so we don't proliferate layout variants in CSS surface APIs.

Jon: noted. I'll rename tokens in the PR and create a migration note in the release notes.

Maya: thanks all — I'll push a small fix and ping for review. :rocket:
